edit.description: `nested_file_path` (1050) stops demanding the host kind's `governs_root` and `unit_shape`: it composes the host's own unit through the same derivation (`member_projection_path`), so a host that is itself a nested-file member with a directory unit supplies an interior and depth is unbounded. A directory-unit child's template path names its entry file the way a directory kind's glob does, and a template cycle in the declared kind graph refuses loud rather than recursing (invariant 6).

`discover_nested_file` (219) recurses: a nested-file host owning a directory unit is itself scanned for the layers it templates, so a child two layers down is discovered rather than invisible; the declared-governed-path carve-out and the host-identity carry travel down with it. `unit_dir` (285) reads a unit one level below a kind's root — a deeper host's unit is below its own host's, not the root's.

`resolve_kind_units`'s nested-file branch (956) is `discover_nested_file`'s one production caller: a recursive walk hands it units whose host is itself a nested-file member, so the host address it qualifies each child's id with is taken off the unit — through `member_address::address_of`, which reads any depth once the grammar entry lands — rather than re-derived as a bare `kind:name`.

`hostUnit` (193) refuses every locus but `at`, so the SDK cannot compose under a nested-file host at all: it composes such a host's unit from the host's own host, keeping the SDK's path derivation in agreement with the engine's at depth.

A two-layer corpus: an `area` directory-unit host templating a `page` directory-unit file child, itself templating a leaf child — projections at `<root>/<a>/<b>/<dir>/<key>.<ext>`, addresses `area:<a>/page/<b>/<kind>/<key>`, and a declared template cycle refusing.
`explain` resolves the two-layer address, composing through both hosts — the member grain the grammar entry opened, now with a corpus behind it.
The frozen-agreement lane gains a two-layer target, so the SDK and engine derivations are gated into agreement at depth, not only at one level.

The equivalence lane builds through `resolve_kind_units` over real Claude Code fixtures with no disk round trip, so the recursion's signature and unit ordering reach it; the fixtures template one layer, so the assertions should stand unchanged — verify rather than assume.

The cost harness walks `discover_nested_file` per kind (1105) and pins glob compilation per distinct glob; a descent per nested layer changes the walk, so the pinned counts and the helper's `(kind, unit.file, unit.host_unit)` read are re-derived against the recursion.

summary: A nested-file member can host a further nested layer: the host's unit composes recursively, so nesting reaches arbitrary depth instead of stopping at one level

tests.asserts: a child two layers down emits at its composed path, carries the two-host-composed address, and a template cycle refuses loud
both derivations agree on a two-layer child's path

acceptance: `cargo test` and `pnpm --dir sdk test` green, with a two-layer corpus emitting, discovering and resolving at both layers, and a self-templating kind refused rather than looping.
notes: Re-scoped off the address-grammar capture: the two address readers and the fold/splice inverse are its three parents, so this entry is composition only — `src/member_address.rs` and `sdk/src/member-address.ts` are the parents' files, and the inner layer may keep a directory-segment pattern because the fold lands first. A multi-segment host name is not the answer: a name is one segment, `/` the separator. No new kind fact — `nested-file` already declares `unitShape`. scoped at 9626a1a6
